+// SparseCraft design point.
+//
+// The SPARSECRAFT lines below are SOFTWARE-side: tiling and the
+// sparsity pattern. They are compiler
+// defines, not Chisel parameters, so they live in comments -- but the harness
+// parses them back out, so they must be kept and kept well-formed.
+// SPARSECRAFT workload = dnn512
+// SPARSECRAFT dense_mode = 0
+// The Gemmini instruction schedule (the software co-design levers). They
+// reach the build as -DSPMM_KCHUNK / -DSPMM_B_BLOCKS.
+//
+// k_chunk stays 16 and that is a CORRECTNESS-adjacent choice, not inertia.
+// K = 256/DIM = 16 blocks, so k_chunk = 16 accumulates the ENTIRE K dimension
+// in a single accumulator-resident pass and the 256x64 int32 output is
+// written to DRAM exactly once (WDMA_BYTES_SENT = 131,072 = 256*64*4*2, i.e.
+// already at the floor for this output). Halving k_chunk to free scratchpad
+// rows would double the accumulator spill/refill traffic, and the energy
+// model prices a DRAM byte at 22 pJ against 0.30 pJ for a MAC -- a 73x ratio.
+// Paying DRAM to buy SRAM is the wrong direction on this workload.
+// SPARSECRAFT k_chunk = 16
+// SPARSECRAFT b_blocks = 0
+// x_resident 0 -> 1 (iteration 2): off_chip_bytes measured at 3,211,264 B, of
+// which RDMA_BYTES_REC = 3,080,192 is the repeated re-fetch of the dense X
+// operand once per K-pass. At 22 pJ/byte that is ~71 of the 95.7 uJ total, so
+// DRAM, not MAC and not SRAM, is the dominant energy term. Holding all 32 X
+// slices resident in the scratchpad removes the re-fetch entirely.
+// MEASURED: cycles 106,650 -> 79,433 (-25.5%), energy 95.7 -> 32.2 uJ (-66.3%),
+// off_chip_bytes 3,211,264 -> 327,680. Confirmed: the DRAM term is now gone.
+// SPARSECRAFT x_resident = 1
+// The four below are RTL-microarchitecture parameters. They are markers, NOT
+// GemminiArrayConfig fields.
+//
+// gate_enable 0 -> 1 (iteration 3).
+// MEASURED: MAC_GATED_TOTAL = 7,864,320 of 8,388,608 issued, so the gate
+// fires on 93.75% of multiplies exactly as predicted -- and energy moved only
+// 32.235 -> 30.111 uJ (-6.6%). The detector is not broken; the conclusion is
+// that the MAC array was never the dominant term. The whole switched
+// multiplier capacity is worth at most ~2.3 uJ. Fmax did not move, so T-A is
+// kept: a pure, paid-for win, but its ceiling is now known and it is small.
+// T-A SCOPE IS SATURATED. The gate already fires on 93.75% of multiplies,
+// which is exactly macs_issued - macs_useful; there is no remaining zero
+// population for a wider gate to catch. Extending the gate to the stationary
+// operand would catch nothing, because the stationary operand is X, which is
+// DENSE. That lever is closed and should not be re-proposed.
+// SPARSECRAFT gate_enable = 1
+//
+// zbu_enable 0 -> 1 (iteration 4). MEASURED -17.5% energy, +4.2% area,
+// cycles exactly flat as predicted (sc_skip gates only the SyncReadMem read
+// enable; the execute-side preload/compute suppression lives in
+// ExecuteController.scala, which is not writable).
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_enable = 1
+//
+// granule_size stays 16 and that is FORCED BY THE WIRING, not chosen.
+// Verified again this iteration by reading the harness-owned tap:
+// Scratchpad.scala line 165 declares `val mem = SyncReadMem(n, Vec(mask_len,
+// mask_elem))` and line 203/206 suppress with `mem.read(raddr, ren &&
+// !sc_skip)`. A SyncReadMem read enable is ONE bit for the WHOLE row. There
+// is no sub-row read enable to drive, so a granule of 8 or 4 could only be
+// consumed by AND-ing its sub-flags back up to a row flag -- bitwise
+// IDENTICAL skips, at 2x/4x the bitmap flops and a deeper reduce in series
+// with the read path. Finer is strictly dominated here: more area, more
+// delay, the same suppressions. Coarser is impossible: granule_size must
+// divide DIM = 16, so 16 is already the maximum. The granularity lever is
+// closed in BOTH directions in this build.
+// SPARSECRAFT granule_size = 16
+// zbu_operand stays A: A is the 93.75%-zero streaming operand. X is dense and
+// resident, so a bitmap over it would never fire.
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_operand = A
+//
+// ================== ITERATION 9: sp_capacity 128 -> 64 KB ===================
+// The measured diagnosis is "balanced, no single bottleneck (exe_active=0.75,
+// dma_wait=0.01)" and it names exactly two sanctioned responses: change the
+// MECHANISM, or "remove capacity the software schedule no longer needs".
+// The mechanism half is closed this iteration and the two notes above say why
+// with evidence rather than assertion -- T-A already gates 93.75% of all
+// multiplies (nothing left to catch, and the stationary operand is dense),
+// and granule_size is pinned at 16 from both sides by the row-granular
+// SyncReadMem read enable. So the actionable response is the capacity half,
+// and the surplus is still enormous.
+//
+// THE OCCUPANCY ARITHMETIC, in scratchpad rows (one row = DIM = 16 INT8 = 16 B):
+//   X resident (x_resident = 1)  32 K-slices x (16 rows x 64 cols / DIM)
+//                                 = 32 x 64                   = 2,048 rows
+//   A staging   k_chunk * DIM     = 16 * 16                   =   256 rows
+//   B staging   k_chunk*(N/DIM)*DIM = 16 * 4 * 16             = 1,024 rows
+//                                                       total = 3,328 rows
+// Available at sp_capacity = 128 KB: 131,072 B / 16 B = 8,192 rows. The live
+// working set is 41% of the array; 4,864 rows are synthesised SRAM that is
+// powered, leaked and charged to area while holding nothing.
+//
+// At 64 KB: 65,536 / 16 = 4,096 rows, 1,024 per bank across sp_banks = 4.
+// T0 check, all four clauses: rows/bank = 1,024 is a power of two and a
+// multiple of DIM = 16; sp_banks = 4 >= 3; the ZBU bitmap is 1,024 bits/bank
+// x 4 banks = 512 B, i.e. 0.8% of the 64 KB budget it must fit inside;
+// Little's Law is untouched (64 x 64 unchanged). The working set of 3,328
+// rows still fits in 4,096 with 768 rows spare, and it PARTITIONS cleanly on
+// the 1,024-row bank boundaries: X in banks 0-1, B in bank 2, A in bank 3.
+// No tile has to be re-staged, k_chunk and x_resident are unchanged, so the
+// instruction schedule is identical and correctness cannot move -- nothing
+// about WHAT is computed changes, only how much unused SRAM sits behind it.
+//
+// WHAT IT BUYS, per axis:
+//  - AREA: the scratchpad macro halves again, and the ZBU bitmap halves WITH
+//    it, because SparseCraftZBU is elaborated with n = rows-per-bank:
+//    2,048 -> 1,024 bits per bank, 8,192 -> 4,096 bitmap flops across four
+//    banks. One lever, two storage structures. The 256 -> 128 step measured
+//    -17.3% area; this step halves the same macro again.
+//  - ENERGY: the residual after DRAM (327,680 B x 22 pJ ~= 7.2 uJ) and the
+//    MAC array (bounded above by the T-A delta, ~2.3 uJ) is ~11 uJ of
+//    scratchpad traffic -- still the single largest term in the 20.951 uJ
+//    total. The model scales per-access SRAM cost as sqrt(max(SRAM,32KB)/256KB)
+//    over scratchpad + accumulator: 192 KB -> 128 KB takes that factor from
+//    sqrt(192/256) = 0.866 to sqrt(128/256) = 0.707, i.e. -18% on EVERY
+//    surviving access. This compounds with T-B rather than competing with it:
+//    T-B removes accesses, this makes the ones that remain cheaper. Note the
+//    32 KB floor -- scratchpad 64 + accumulator 64 = 128 KB is still well
+//    above it, so the full sqrt benefit is available and is not yet clipped.
+//  - ACCUMULATOR HELD AT 64 KB DELIBERATELY. The 256x64 int32 output tile is
+//    exactly 65,536 B, so acc_capacity = 64 KB is the working set, not slack.
+//    Shrinking it would force a second output pass and pay DRAM for SRAM.
+//  - FMAX, hence t: the ZBU read path is bitmap(read_addr) feeding
+//    mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip) -- a register-file mux in SERIES with
+//    the SRAM read enable. 2,048:1 -> 1,024:1 removes another mux level from
+//    that path, and the SRAM macro is faster at half the depth. t = cycles x
+//    MEASURED period, so that is where a time win would come from. The 256 ->
+//    128 step also returned cycles 79,433 -> 50,862 (-36%), which I did not
+//    predict as a cycle effect and still cannot attribute to the schedule
+//    (off_chip_bytes was bit-identical at 327,680 either side of it); I am
+//    therefore NOT banking a repeat of that and predict cycles flat.
+// ============================================================================
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+
+object SparseCraftParams {
+  val config = GemminiConfigs.defaultConfig.copy(
+    // --- L2 PE array geometry ---
+    // DIM = meshRows * tileRows = 16 and it is PINNED to the kernel: spmm.c
+    // defines DIM_ = SPMM_DIM = 16 from spmm_data.h and mixes it with the
+    // elaborated DIM in the same pointer arithmetic. Iteration 5 moved this
+    // to 32 and produced 32,674 mismatching outputs. Do not move it alone.
+    meshRows    = 16,
+    meshColumns = 16,
+    tileRows    = 1,
+    tileColumns = 1,
+    dataflow    = Dataflow.WS,
+
+    // --- L3 scratchpad / accumulator ---
+    // 128 -> 64 KB (iteration 9). 4,096 rows / 1,024 per bank against a
+    // measured live working set of 3,328 rows. See the note above.
+    sp_capacity     = CapacityInKilobytes(64),
+    acc_capacity    = CapacityInKilobytes(64),
+    sp_banks        = 4,
+    acc_banks       = 2,
+    spad_read_delay = 4,
+    acc_latency     = 2,
+
+    // --- L5 address generation / DMA ---
+    max_in_flight_mem_reqs = 64,
+    dma_maxbytes           = 64,
+    dma_buswidth           = 128,
+    tlb_size               = 4,
+
+    // --- L7 RoCC / queueing surface ---
+    ld_queue_length = 8,
+    st_queue_length = 2,
+    ex_queue_length = 8,
+    reservation_station_entries_ld = 8,
+    reservation_station_entries_st = 4,
+    reservation_station_entries_ex = 16,
+
+    // --- L10 numerics / nonlinear ---
+    has_normalizations = true,
+    mvin_scale_shared  = false,
+
+    // --- profiling ---
+    num_counter = 8,
+
+    // --- leanConfig deltas, kept explicit ---
+    // TRUE, not false. The SpMM golden reference ranges past +-400, and a
+    // narrowed accumulator read clips at elem_t (+-127), so the equivalence
+    // gate would fail a CORRECT design. The kernel passes full_C=true and

+// See README.md for license details.
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+
+/** Zero-Bitmap Unit (ZBU) -- T-B: zero-granule skipping.
+  *
+  * ==== INTERFACE -- THIS PORT LIST IS A CONTRACT ====
+  *
+  * Scratchpad.scala is harness-owned and instantiates this module verbatim.
+  * It will not adapt to a changed port list, so renaming or re-typing a port
+  * fails elaboration. Everything INSIDE the module is yours.
+  *
+  *   n   rows in the bank -- one bitmap bit per row
+  *   w   row width in bits
+  *
+  *   io.write_fire  Input  Bool       a write is landing this cycle
+  *   io.write_addr  Input  UInt       its row
+  *   io.write_data  Input  UInt(w.W)  its data
+  *   io.write_full  Input  Bool       the write covers the WHOLE row
+  *   io.read_addr   Input  UInt       the row being read this cycle
+  *   io.read_en     Input  Bool       a read is being issued this cycle
+  *   io.skip        Output Bool       this read may be skipped: row is zero
+  *
+  * ==== SEMANTICS THE HARNESS RELIES ON ====
+  *
+  *  - `skip` may be high ONLY when the row is KNOWN to be entirely zero.
+  *  - A partial (masked) write must CLEAR the bit. Conservative is correct.
+  *
+  * ==================== DESIGN NOTES (iteration 4) ====================
+  *
+  * GRANULE = w bits = DIM elements = one row, and that is not a free choice
+  * here, it is forced by the wiring. Scratchpad.scala suppresses the read with
+  *
+  *     mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip)
+  *
+  * `mem` is a SyncReadMem whose read enable is ONE bit for the WHOLE row.
+  * There is no sub-row read enable to drive, so a granule finer than the row
+  * could only be consumed by AND-ing all the sub-granule flags of a row back
+  * together -- which is bitwise identical to the row flag, at 2x/4x/16x the
+  * bitmap area and a deeper reduce. Finer granularity in THIS build is
+  * strictly dominated: more area, more delay, exactly the same skips. Hence
+  * granule_size stays at 16 (= DIM = one row) and the lever I actually move
+  * is detector pipeline depth, below.
+  *
+  * DETECTOR PIPELINE DEPTH (the real change vs. the seed).
+  * The seed did the whole detector in the write cycle:
+  *
+  *     when (write_fire) { bitmap(write_addr) := write_full && (write_data === 0.U) }
+  *
+  * which puts a w-wide (128b) OR-reduce IN SERIES with a 4096-entry one-hot
+  * write decoder inside a single cycle, and the bitmap is a flat register file
+  * whose 4096:1 read mux already sits in series with the SRAM read enable.
+  * Both halves of the ZBU landed on the same clock period, and Fmax is the
+  * axis T-B is most likely to lose on -- t is cycles x MEASURED period, so an
+  * energy win paid for in period is not a win.
+  *
+  * So the detector is split into two stages: cycle 0 reduces the data and
+  * latches (addr, bit); cycle 1 commits it into the bitmap. The OR-reduce and
+  * the write decoder are now in different cycles.
+  *
+  * WHY THE PIPELINE IS STILL BIT-EXACT.
+  * A one-cycle-late bitmap update creates exactly one hazard: a read issued in
+  * the shadow cycle sees the PRE-write bit. If the pending write is making a
+  * previously-zero row NONZERO, that stale bit is SET and we would skip a read
+  * of real data -- silent corruption, the exact failure mode the header warns
+  * about. `hazard` kills the skip for any read whose address matches the
+  * in-flight write, so the shadow cycle degrades to "read it densely", which
+  * is always safe. The converse case (pending write makes the row zero, we
+  * fail to skip) costs one missed skip and cannot corrupt.
+  * The comparator sits in PARALLEL with the bitmap mux, not in series, so it
+  * adds one 2-input AND to the read path, not a second mux tree.
+  *
+  * The bit is set only on a FULL-WIDTH all-zero write. A masked write clears
+  * it unconditionally -- the row is then partly unknown, and "unknown" must
+  * read as "not provably zero".
+  */
+class SparseCraftZBU(n: Int, w: Int) extends Module {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    val write_fire = Input(Bool())
+    val write_addr = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val write_data = Input(UInt(w.W))
+    val write_full = Input(Bool())
+    val read_addr  = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val read_en    = Input(Bool())
+    val skip       = Output(Bool())
+  })
+
+  // One bit per row. At granule_size = DIM a row IS a granule.
+  // RESET VALUE IS false = "not provably zero" = conservative. A bitmap that
+  // comes out of reset all-ones would skip reads of rows that were never
+  // written, which is the corruption case.
+  val bitmap = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(n)(false.B)))
+
+  // ---- stage 0: detect. w-wide OR-reduce, ends at a flop. ----
+  // `!orR` rather than `=== 0.U` so the reduce is emitted as a balanced tree
+  // instead of a w-bit equality against a constant.
+  val row_is_zero = !io.write_data.orR
+  val new_bit     = io.write_full && row_is_zero
+
+  val pend_valid = RegNext(io.write_fire, false.B)
+  val pend_addr  = RegEnable(io.write_addr, io.write_fire)
+  val pend_bit   = RegEnable(new_bit,       io.write_fire)
+
+  // ---- stage 1: commit. One-hot decode over n entries, starts at a flop. ----
+  when (pend_valid) {
+    bitmap(pend_addr) := pend_bit
+  }
+
+  // ---- read: bitmap lookup, with the shadow-cycle write hazard suppressed. ----
+  val hazard = pend_valid && (pend_addr === io.read_addr)
+
+  io.skip := bitmap(io.read_addr) && io.read_en && !hazard
+}
